chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb, who said, 'Jameel narrated to me saying, I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'
'Is there a prescribed supplication that I should say upon As-Safa and Al-Marwa?'
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say when you stand upon As-Safa:'
There is no god except Allah Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Able over all things.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed supplication to recite on As-Safa during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the specific liturgical formula for the pause (wuquf) on As-Safa, emphasizing the attributes of divine sovereignty and power through the repetition of 'La ilaha illa Allah...'. In Shia scholarly tradition, this practice is viewed as a reenactment of Hajar’s devotion, linking the physical ritual to spiritual affirmation of God’s absolute control over life and death. The instruction to recite it three times underscores the importance of deliberate, repetitive dhikr in solidifying faith during the pilgrimage rites.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said, ‘Jameel narrated to me saying,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there any from a prescribed supplication which I should be saying upon Al-Safa and Al-Marwa?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying when you pause upon Al-Safa:

‘There is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Alone, there being no associates for him. For Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Kingdom, and for Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Praise. He<sup>azwj</sup> Revives and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to die, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Able upon everything
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following: “Jamil narrated to me saying, ‘I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, “
Is there a prayer of a particular timing that I should say at al-Safa’ and al-Marwah?”
No one other than Allah, who is One and has no partners, deserves worship. To Him belong the kingdom and all praise. He gives life and causes things to die and has power over all things
